{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.2 (Site Development and Hosting Agreement)

**To:** Deal team
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)
**Re:** Playbook review of the HDI Site Development and Hosting Agreement — verified findings only

## Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against our playbook. HDI is the vendor: it designs, develops, hosts, operates and promotes the Site and performs "Services" for us, yet the Agreement is silent on the three protections we treat as non-negotiable. There is **no indemnification** of any kind, **no limitation of liability or damages exclusion**, and **no IP ownership or data-ownership provision** — meaning we fund the Site through a revenue share and a Termination Payment without confirmed ownership of the deliverables, our Content or the customer data, and with unlimited mutual exposure. We propose a vendor indemnity (new § 9(c)), a mutual cap with uncapped Excluded Claims (new § 10.9), and an ownership section.

The second cluster of issues is the exit economics. Section 4.2(a) imposes a Termination Payment of 50% of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000 on *any* termination by us — including termination for HDI's own non-performance — against fees of only 30% of Net Sales. Combined with § 6.1's exclusive dealing covenant (Deerskin Products and "substantially similar" products, sweeping in third-party competitor lines) and § 4.1's 90-day, renewal-only notice window, we are effectively locked in for the full term with no performance-based exit. We have taken playbook fallbacks rather than outright deletion, recognising that HDI funds the build, hosting and promotion.

Remaining items are more contained: HDI's uncapped inspection right (§ 3.4), the missing venue designation under the otherwise-acceptable New York governing law clause (§ 10.5), the narrow § 1.4 access grant, the absence of transition assistance and data return, the absence of a performance warranty, and the absence of vendor insurance. Two points are already compliant or require no edit: there is no MFN burdening us (and § 1.8's "no less favorably" promotion covenant runs in our favour), and there is no non-solicit binding us — though that finding did not pass verification and should be re-run before we rely on it.

## Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Issue / proposal |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | § 5.4 (insertion point: new § 9(c)) | No indemnity, defence or hold-harmless language anywhere; § 7.2 is a covenant only. Add HDI indemnity for third-party IP claims, breach of law, HDI-caused data incidents and misconduct, carving out Company-provided Content and Marks. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Missing | Preamble / Agreement-wide | No ownership or assignment provision; § 10.2 is a partnership carve-out, not an IP allocation. Add: Company owns Site deliverables, Content, Marks and customer data; HDI retains its platform with a perpetual licence back; no joint ownership. |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Missing | § 5.4 (insertion point: new § 10.9) | No cap, no damages exclusion; unlimited direct and consequential exposure both ways. Add mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' § 3 fees or USD 1,000,000, mutual consequential-damages exclusion, uncapped Excluded Claims, and confirmation that our payment/Termination Payment obligations are not "damages". |
| 4 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 1.4 (operative: §§ 4.1, 4.2(a)) | No mid-term convenience exit for us; HDI's mirror 90-day right could be exercised mid-term; § 4.2(a) penalty applies even on our termination for HDI's fault. Add 30-day Company convenience right with refund of prepaid fees, confine HDI's convenience right to end-of-term non-renewal, cap the Termination Payment at three months' fees with a fault-based carve-out. |
| 5 | High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Deviation | § 1.4 (operative: § 4.2) | Termination Payment is uncapped, unrelated to fees payable, and triggered by any termination by us. Fallback taken: single early-termination fee capped at three months' § 3.1 fees, payable only on termination for convenience and not under § 1.6 or for HDI's breach. |
| 6 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation | § 5.4 (operative: § 6.1) | Exclusive dealing for the full auto-renewing term with no performance-based exit — our walk-away position. Fallback taken: confine to Deerskin Products for a fixed 12 months, terminating automatically on HDI's failure to meet service levels, availability requirements or delivery dates (including the § 1.6 launch date). HDI's reciprocal covenant (§ 6.3) and the § 6.2 closeout carve-out are left untouched. |
| 7 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Deviation | § 5.4 (operative: § 6.1) | Field-of-use restriction extends to "products substantially similar to Deerskin Products," expressly sweeping in third-party competitor lines, with no carve-out for internal development or acquired businesses. Fallback taken: limit to a self-contained "Deerskin"-branded consumer web site, term-only, with carve-outs for other channels, internal development and acquisitions. |
| 8 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 5.4 (operative: § 10.3) | Bare successors-and-assigns clause: no customer affiliate/successor carve-out, no restriction on HDI assigning (including to a Deerskin competitor), no change-of-control provision. Add affiliate/successor carve-out for us, consent standard on HDI (not unreasonably withheld, never to a competitor), and confirmation that our change of control is not an assignment and gives HDI no exit. |
| 9 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Deviation | § 1.4 (operative: § 4.1) | One-year renewal length is acceptable, but the 90-day exit notice is three times our preferred window and beyond the 60-day fallback. Shorten our notice to 30 days (leaving HDI's at 90 days) and add a 60-day renewal reminder from HDI; 60 days for our notice is acceptable. No price-increase cap needed (fixed 30% revenue share). |
| 10 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume restrictions | Deviation | § 1.4 (operative: § 4.2(a)) | No minimum spend (fees are a pure revenue share), but the volume-based Termination Payment penalises our only exit route. Fallback taken: keep the negotiated payment but carve out termination for HDI's material breach and termination under § 1.6 (which already contemplates termination "without penalty"). |
| 11 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty | Missing | § 5.4 (insertion point: new § 9(c)) | § 9 is limited to mutual corporate authority representations plus a Globix carve-out; no workmanlike-services, conformance or remedy provision. Add workmanlike Services, 12-month Site conformance, legal compliance and no-malicious-code warranties with a repair/re-performance/refund remedy (90/30-day fallback noted). No "AS IS" disclaimer to displace. |
| 12 | Medium | TRANSITION — Exit assistance and data return | Missing | § 1.4 (insertion point: new § 4.3) | HDI holds our Content, user information and order/export files, but nothing requires return, deletion or migration assistance. Insert up to six months of transition assistance at HDI's then-current rates, machine-readable data return within 30 days, and certified deletion thereafter. |
| 13 | Medium | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 1.4 | The only grant in our favour names "the Company" alone, excluding affiliates and the contractors who would operate the Site, and is revocable at will. Extend to affiliates and contractors, make it non-revocable absent our uncured material breach, and add successor coverage (fallback: affiliate coverage on written notice plus successor transfer). The Marks licence we grant HDI (§ 6.1) needs no change. |
| 14 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | § 1.4 (operative: § 3.4) | HDI's inspection right already gives 30 days' notice, business hours and HDI-borne costs, but is unlimited in frequency with no confidentiality requirement and no systems carve-out. Cap at once per 12 months, require an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, off-site where practicable, and bar direct or remote system access. We deliberately omit the >5% cost-shift, as unconditional HDI cost allocation is better for us. |
| 15 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 5.4 (operative: § 10.5) | New York law is our preferred choice and there is no arbitration or foreign venue provision, but no forum is specified. Add exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County, leaving the governing law wording untouched. |
| 16 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | § 5.4 (insertion point: new § 10.9) | No insurance provision anywhere, despite HDI hosting on its own servers with access to our Confidential Information, Content and Site user information. Add CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, statutory workers' compensation, and certificates on request (fallback: E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M). |
| 17 | Medium | MFN — MFN burdening Customer | Compliant | § 1.4 (§§ 3.1–3.4, § 1.8) | No MFN or best-terms obligation runs against us; § 6.1 is an exclusivity covenant, not an MFN. § 1.8's "no less favorably" promotion covenant runs in our favour and is not redlined. No action. |
| 18 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Needs review (verification failed) | § 5.4 | Finding records no non-solicit, no-hire or inducement covenant anywhere, so the preferred position is met and no edit is proposed. **Verification did not pass** — re-run before relying on this conclusion. |

## Walk-away items

The following sit at or beyond our walk-away boundaries and should be treated as conditions to signature:

1. **No indemnity and no liability cap (Findings 1 and 3).** We cannot sign a hosting agreement under which the vendor designs, hosts and promotes the Site, holds our data, and bears no duty to defend us against third-party IP or data claims, with unlimited exposure running both ways. Both gaps must be filled.
2. **No IP or data ownership (Finding 2).** We fund the Site through the revenue share and Termination Payment; confirmed Company ownership of the deliverables, Content, Marks and customer data — with no joint ownership — is required.
3. **Exclusivity for the full term with no performance exit (Finding 6).** § 6.1 exclusive dealing, coupled with § 4.1's auto-renewal and § 4.2's Termination Payment, is our walk-away position. At minimum we need the fixed 12-month term and automatic release on HDI's performance failure.
4. **Termination Payment triggered by HDI's own breach (Findings 4, 5 and 10).** A payment of roughly 50% of annual Net Sales against fees of 30% of Net Sales, payable even when we terminate for HDI's non-performance or failure to launch, is not acceptable in any form. The fault-based carve-out is not tradeable.
5. **90-day renewal notice (Finding 9).** The current window sits at the walk-away boundary; 60 days is our floor.

## Next steps

1. Issue the redline reflecting the proposals above: new § 9(c) (indemnity and warranty), new § 10.9 (liability cap and insurance), new § 4.3 (transition and data return), the ownership section, and amendments to §§ 1.4, 3.4, 4.1, 4.2, 6.1, 10.3 and 10.5. Confirm that the § 10.7 survival clause captures each new provision as intended.
2. Re-run verification on the NOSOLICIT finding (Finding 18) and confirm the absence of any hiring restriction before we close that item.
3. Have the deal team price the § 4.2(a) Termination Payment against projected Net Sales so we can quantify the exposure we are trading away in the three-month fee cap fallback.
4. Confirm with the business which product lines and channels must sit outside § 6.1 (other channels, internal development, acquisitions) so the non-compete carve-outs are drafted to the right scope.
5. Note for the deal team, outside the NOSOLICIT rule: HDI's exclusivity covenant runs for the term plus two years and survives under § 10.7, while ours is term-only. That asymmetry favours us and should be preserved when negotiating § 6.1.
6. Convene a 30-minute call with the business sponsor on the walk-away items before we send the markup, so our position on the exit economics is aligned."}
